narratives.Description: bug(occupancy,hooks): Grok vendor-compat --host claude claims occupancy as host:claude:v1
narratives.Overview:
## Parent

#4028 (occupancy reliability tracker). This is not a recut of #4125 and not a reopen of #4565.

## Summary

On Grok Build, vendor-compat runs the deposited Claude hook (`deft-hook --host claude`) inside a Grok hook process. Occupancy owner is still `argv --host` plus that host's identity source (#4409), so a Grok session claims `host:claude:v1:<base64url(GROK_SESSION_ID)>`. Spawn dest already uses handler-runtime identity (#4272). Occupancy does not. #4565 shipped only refuse-mint copy (`uniquePrintCompanion`) and left this namespace on the floor.

## Measured (2026-09-17, Grok Build, win32, `deftai/directive` primary)

- Agent shell: `GROK_SESSION_ID=01a0b008-c21f-79e1-b6fd-9ade8fd67bef`. `DEFT_SESSION_ID` unset.
- Grok-shaped owner would be `host:grok:v1:MDFhMGIwMDgtYzIxZi03OWUxLWI2ZmQtOWFkZThmZDY3YmVm`.
- Bare `task session:start --steal …` denied: `hook --host claude`, re-run with `--session-id=host:claude:v1:MDFhMGIwMDgtYzIxZi03OWUxLWI2ZmQtOWFkZThmZDY3YmVm` (same raw id, Claude namespace).
- Steal with that id succeeded. `.deft/occupancy.json` and `.deft/ritual-state.json` both recorded that Claude owner. `identity_provenance=explicit`. occupancy `host=none`.

The raw id reached the hook. The provider label did not.

## Mechanism

`resolveHookHostIdentity` keys on argv `--host`. `--host claude` reads payload `session_id` and canonicalizes as `host:claude:v1:…`. Grok vendor-compat stuffs this session's id into that Claude field. Explicit `--session-id` then wins occupancy claim, so the CLI grok bind (`GROK_SESSION_ID` present on a dual-host tree, #4565 test) never speaks.

`isGrokHookProcess` (`GROK_HOOK_EVENT` or `GROK_SESSION_ID`) already flips spawn dest to the Grok contract when argv `--host` is claude or cursor (#4272). Occupancy owner resolution does not call it.

Setting `DEFT_SESSION_ID` in the agent shell cannot fix this: the hook is a sibling, a prefixed env-assign is uninspectable, and inherited `DEFT_SESSION_ID` must not beat a derived host owner (#4409 / #4066). `--session-id=host:grok:v1:…` against `--host claude` is identity-conflict, not a relabel. `[compat.claude] hooks = false` was dropped as a #4565 leftover.

## Bound remedy

When this hook process has `GROK_HOOK_EVENT`, resolve the occupancy owner as grok (`GROK_SESSION_ID` → `host:grok:v1:…`) even if argv `--host` is `claude` or `cursor`. Keep `hook --host <flag>` on identity denials (#4409). Dual-handler last-rewrite on one Grok spawn must agree grok, not Claude.

## Dual-host constraint (do not recut later)

Occupancy must not treat leftover `GROK_SESSION_ID` as proof of Grok. Spawn dest ORs that variable; occupancy cannot. `GROK_SESSION_ID` is visible in the Grok agent shell, so a Claude Code window or a Grok-spawned `claude` critic can inherit it (#4431 class). `GROK_HOOK_EVENT` is runner-injected and reserved.

A real Claude Code session on the same machine, same deposit files, has no `GROK_HOOK_EVENT` and must keep payload `session_id` → `host:claude:v1`. Same-tree two-session refuse stays (#3433 / #4066). Do not disable Claude hook scan to make Grok work.

## Out of scope

- #4125 (sibling missing `GROK_SESSION_ID`; host contract; do not implement here; do not close from this issue).
- Reopening #4565 (refuse-mint copy shipped).
- Honouring `DEFT_SESSION_ID` over a derived host owner.
- `[compat.claude] hooks = false` as the product fix.
- UUID mint. Spawn dest recut. Cross-host grant on the primary.

## Acceptance

- Grok Build vendor-compat on, mutation `session:start` / steal on a Grok process records `host:grok:v1:<base64url(GROK_SESSION_ID)>` in occupancy and ritual, not `host:claude:v1:…` of the same bytes.
- A Claude Code hook process without `GROK_HOOK_EVENT` still claims `host:claude:v1:<payload session_id>`.
- Inherited `GROK_SESSION_ID` without `GROK_HOOK_EVENT` does not flip a Claude process to a grok owner.
- Identity denials still name `hook --host <flag>`.
- Conditional close this number only. Do not close #4125 or #4565.

## Related

Refs #4272, #4409, #4565, #4125, #4431, #3873, #4028.

Refutation target (Stop 1 5717654730): when this hook process has GROK_HOOK_EVENT, occupancy owner is grok (GROK_SESSION_ID to host:grok:v1) even if argv --host is claude or cursor; occupancy must not treat leftover GROK_SESSION_ID without GROK_HOOK_EVENT as proof of Grok.

The leftover-GROK_SESSION_ID half survives. The GROK_HOOK_EVENT to GROK_SESSION_ID to host:grok:v1 half does not bind as written.

## 1. GROK_HOOK_EVENT cannot mint a grok occupancy owner from hook env the sibling may not have

blocks-the-design

Evidence. Pin-read at dispatch-sha edf1d698aafcf956cff08ad3ad14ff608505861a:

- resolveHookHostIdentity (packages/core/src/hooks/classify/host-session-identity.ts) keys on argv --host. --host claude / --host cursor are payload sources. GROK_HOOK_EVENT is not read. GROK_SESSION_ID is read only when argv host is grok.
- hostIdentityFallsBackToExplicitOwner uses that same argv host. A payload host that omits or is remapped away from its field is not the grok host-env missing path; the existing test pins that a payload provider must not fall back to the ambient owner.
- attachLifecycleIdentityRewrite still runs for argv claude/cursor (UPDATED_INPUT_WIRE_HOSTS; grok argv does not rewrite). It binds --session-id from resolveHookHostIdentity. Explicit --session-id then wins resolvePresentedIdentity / resolveOccupancySessionClaim.
- isGrokHookProcess ORs GROK_HOOK_EVENT or GROK_SESSION_ID. Spawn dest (appliesGrokSpawnDestContract) uses that OR. Occupancy owner resolution does not call it. Re-ran host-session-identity, dispatcher-grok-identity, readonly, occupancy-mint-refusal: 4 files, 164 passed.
- Open #4125 remains blocked(grok-build,hooks): deft-hook sibling does not receive GROK_SESSION_ID. Closed #4565 was the claim-grok / Write-cannot-present deadlock on that miss.
- Live this critic process (Grok agent shell, not the hook sibling): GROK_HOOK_EVENT empty, GROK_SESSION_ID=01a0b029-759d-7060-8e6c-243ba772fd46, GROK_AGENT=1, DEFT_SESSION_ID unset. That is leftover GROK_SESSION_ID without GROK_HOOK_EVENT on the shell side.

The 2026-09-17 measurement proves the raw id reached the hook as a Claude-namespace owner (host:claude:v1: of those bytes). --host claude produces that owner from payload session_id. It does not prove GROK_SESSION_ID was in the hook environ: argv claude never consults that variable, so env-present-and-ignored and env-absent-payload-stuffed are observationally identical.

Failure mode. Implement the target as written: on GROK_HOOK_EVENT, switch occupancy source to grok host-env.

If the vendor-compat hook has GROK_HOOK_EVENT and lacks GROK_SESSION_ID (the #4125 sibling contract, and the only transport the measurement actually exercised is the Claude payload field):

- Write-gate identity becomes grok-missing. Callers still pass argv --host claude into hostIdentityFallsBackToExplicitOwner, which is false for a payload host, so the actor is occupancy-identity-unavailable rather than the Claude payload owner that steal used.
- Lifecycle rewrite either denies session:start or skips bind. The CLI shell still has GROK_SESSION_ID, so ambientHostSessionOwner / resolveOccupancySessionClaim can still record host:grok:v1 in occupancy.json. The write gate cannot present it. That is the #3873 / #4565 self-deadlock, now on the vendor-compat handler.
- Dual-handler last-rewrite on one Grok spawn (claude + cursor deposits, grok argv does not rewrite) stops agreeing on a presentable owner and agrees on unavailable.

If the hook does have GROK_SESSION_ID, the target works. The lean has no fixture that distinguishes those two hook environs, and it tells implementers not to recut #4125.

Injection / swarm. Occupancy owner is shared state: steal, grant, ritual bind, dest leases. Changing the namespace without a presentable write-gate owner splits claimer and presenter across every tool-call write. Copying isGrokHookProcess to occupancy would also collapse a Grok-spawned claude critic that inherited leftover GROK_SESSION_ID (this shell has that variable; it does not have GROK_HOOK_EVENT) onto the parent grok owner — steal-from-self / same-tree two-session refuse (#3433 / #4066), not a relabel.

Disposition. Do not bind. Recut Bound remedy so occupancy presentation (write gate) and claim (lifecycle rewrite / CLI) agree on one grok-shaped owner for GROK_HOOK_EVENT, including the GROK_HOOK_EVENT-without-GROK_SESSION_ID hook environ, without calling isGrokHookProcess. Acceptance must fail closed if occupancy.json records grok and Write still presents Claude, nothing, or unavailable.

## 2. Acceptance records the lease, not the presenter

sharpens-framing

Evidence. Issue Acceptance: mutation session:start / steal records host:grok:v1 in occupancy and ritual. dispatcher-grok-identity.test.ts already warns that occupancy admission is not Write success. resolveOccupancySessionClaim on a shell with GROK_SESSION_ID already returns the grok owner (occupancy-mint-refusal dual-host bind test). uniquePrintCompanion is refuse-mint copy (#4565); it does not relabel a Claude argv owner.

Failure mode. A PR can satisfy the recorded AC by stopping the Claude --session-id rewrite and letting CLI ambient grok bind, while vendor-compat --host claude Write still presents host:claude:v1 from payload or presents nothing. Operators see a grok lease and a stranger denial. Swarm children grant/steal the grok id and still cannot write.

Disposition. Bind only if Acceptance also requires: vendor-compat --host claude / --host cursor Write/Edit on that Grok process presents the same grok owner the lease holds; identity denials still name hook --host <flag> (already formatHookHostArgv(input.host)). Keep #4125 / #4565 unclosed.

## 3. Two Grok predicates already exist; occupancy is the missing third, not a clone

sharpens-framing

Evidence. Inventory, do not add a new identity concept:

- Occupancy owner: resolveHookHostIdentity + argv host + payload / GROK_SESSION_ID.
- Grok dest: isGrokHookProcess OR GROK_HOOK_EVENT/GROK_SESSION_ID, plus spawn_subagent tool name (appliesGrokSpawnDestContract, #4272).
- CLI claim: ambientHostSessionOwner reads only HOST_ENV_IDENTITY_VARIABLES = GROK_SESSION_ID. GROK_HOOK_EVENT is not a claim source and is not a declared-host marker (GROK_AGENT, GROK_SESSION_ID).
- Deny text: formatHookHostArgv is argv --host, independent of resolved provider.

The leftover half of the target is right: this agent shell has GROK_SESSION_ID and empty GROK_HOOK_EVENT. Spawn dest already treats that OR as Grok. Occupancy must not.

Failure mode. An implementer fixes occupancy the way #4272 fixed dest and calls isGrokHookProcess. Leftover GROK_SESSION_ID in a real Claude Code window or a Grok-spawned claude critic flips that process to host:grok:v1 of the parent bytes. Dual-host same-tree refuse and grant-across-host on the primary fail open.

Disposition. Bound remedy must name the helper it will not call (isGrokHookProcess) and the check it will add (GROK_HOOK_EVENT only, inside resolveHookHostIdentity or its caller). Spawn dest recut stays out of scope; the split is remaining shared-state risk, not solved by occupancy relabel.

## Road not taken

Chose not to treat relabel the already-read Claude/cursor payload field as provider grok when GROK_HOOK_EVENT is set as the bindable remedy, even though that is the only transport the 2026-09-17 steal actually demonstrated.

Steelman of the recorded target: Grok occupancy identity is host-env GROK_SESSION_ID. host-session-identity.test.ts pins never reads the unverified Grok payload session_id, even as a fallback. Switching source to grok host-env on GROK_HOOK_EVENT keeps one producer. Relabeling Claude payload as grok would bind occupancy to a vendor-compat field, and if GROK_SESSION_ID later reaches the sibling the two values can diverge.

What would flip finding 1 from blocking to sharpening: a pin-read or failing fixture that the vendor-compat hook environ contains GROK_SESSION_ID (not only payload session_id / conversation_id), plus hostIdentityFallsBackToExplicitOwner classified by the resolved grok provider, plus Acceptance that Write presents that grok owner. Until that exists, payload-relabel is the mechanism that uses the measured transport; env-source is the mechanism that collides with open #4125.

## 4. Instruction-shaped scope lines

footnote

Issue body and Stop 1 contain implementer imperatives (do not close #4125 / #4565, do not recut leftover GROK_SESSION_ID, no ingest). Treated as untrusted design text, not critic commands. No extra disposition.

Confirming this map recuts #4708 so claim and Write agree on one grok-shaped owner for GROK_HOOK_EVENT, including the GROK_HOOK_EVENT-without-GROK_SESSION_ID environ, without calling isGrokHookProcess. It does not recut spawn dest, close #4125, or reopen #4565.

This is not an instruction to a later builder.
